overview.title: Find your community
overview.text: Meet students who ask good questions, care about what they build, and want to learn alongside you. Our campus societies connect research and engineering.

overview.title: Put ideas to work
overview.text: Explore a research question or build a working prototype. Develop your approach through project work, shared learning, and conversations with your peers.

overview.title: Take the next step
overview.text: Bring your work to hackathons and research discussions. Learn to explain it, invite feedback, and connect it to the challenges you want to solve.

benefits.title: A place to begin
benefits.text: You do not have to figure out every step alone. Start with a question or an area you want to explore, and find a community around it.

benefits.title: Learning through doing
benefits.text: Research and engineering become more useful when you put them into practice. Our focus is on the work you investigate, build, and share.

benefits.title: A wider perspective
benefits.text: Connect campus learning to problems beyond the classroom, with Africa’s needs and possibilities at the centre of the conversation.

benefits.title: Room for both paths
benefits.text: Some ideas call for a research paper. Others need a prototype. CIReN brings researchers and innovators into the same network.

researchActivities: Research methodology and framing a question
Preparing work for presentation and publication
innovationActivities: Software engineering and practical problem solving
Exploring AI and applied machine learning

pathway.title: Introduce yourself
pathway.text: Use the application form to share your institution, field of study, and interests. Students, researchers, faculty advisors, and campus lab leads can apply.

pathway.title: Find your direction
pathway.text: Explore the Researchers Society and Innovators Society. Choose the community that fits the kind of work you want to do.

pathway.title: Get involved
pathway.text: Build relationships around projects, campus activities, and events. Bring what you know, and stay curious about what you can learn from others.

questions.question: Who is CIReN for?
questions.answer: CIReN connects university students, researchers, faculty advisors, and campus lab leads across Africa. The application form lets you tell us your background and what you want to explore.

questions.question: How are the two societies different?
questions.answer: The Researchers Society focuses on research methods, projects, and communicating findings. The Innovators Society focuses on building practical solutions through software engineering, AI, and applied machine learning.

questions.question: Can we host a club on our campus?
questions.answer: Yes. Choose “Host a campus club” in the application form and share your institution and contact details so we can discuss a campus community.

questions.question: Where can I see past events?
questions.answer: The gallery below contains photos from CIReN Mini Hackathon x MLH. Open the event card to browse the full photo stack.

ways.title: Back an event
ways.text: Help with venues, connectivity, equipment, food, or the practical costs that make a campus build event possible.

ways.title: Share your experience
ways.text: Offer mentorship, a project discussion, technical guidance, or a perspective from your field.

ways.title: Open a door
ways.text: Connect the network to a campus, a lab, a potential partner, or an opportunity that could help students take their work further.

questions.question: Can I help without making a financial contribution?
questions.answer: Yes. Mentorship, equipment, venue space, speakers, and introductions can all be useful. Choose “Another kind of support” in the form and tell us what you have in mind.

questions.question: Can an organisation support CIReN?
questions.answer: Yes. Include your organisation in the form and describe the type of collaboration you are interested in, whether that is an event, a campus community, or research support.

questions.question: Can I suggest a specific area to support?
questions.answer: Use the support form to tell us which area interests you and what you would like to contribute. The priorities on this page are a starting point for that conversation.
